chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Husayn reported to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, he said: Ayyub ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, may God have mercy on him, from Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon them both)

that he said one day to his companions: "O my brothers! I enjoin upon you the abode of the Hereafter, and I do not enjoin upon you the abode of this world, for indeed you are greedy for it and cling to it. Has there not reached you what Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon her) said to the disciples?

He said to them: This world is a bridge, so cross it and do not build upon it. And he said: Which of you builds a house upon the waves of the sea? That is the abode of this world, so do not take it as a permanent place."

key_terms.الآخرة: The Hereafter, the eternal abode after death
key_terms.الحواريين: The disciples of Prophet Isa (Jesus), the Apostles
key_terms.قنطرة: A bridge, crossing point -- metaphor for the transient nature of worldly life

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the nature of this world?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) addressed his followers in an intimate gathering, urging them to focus on the Hereafter rather than worldly attachments. He illustrated this with a famous saying attributed to Prophet Isa (Jesus, AS), comparing the world to a bridge that should be crossed but not settled upon, and to building a house on sea waves -- both vivid metaphors for the futility of worldly attachment. This teaching, delivered in early 2nd-century Hijri Medina, reflects the ascetic tradition that Imam al-Sajjad was particularly known for.
